quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #2
										  					
  

35 Questions • Passing Score 28

questions.question: If your vehicle has a two-part safety belt system, what should you do?

options.text: Use both the lap and shoulder belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the lap and shoulder belts.
questions.explanation: Always wear both the lap belt and shoulder belt. Using only one part greatly reduces your protection. If you have an automatic shoulder belt, also buckle your lap belt.

questions.question: Like alcohol and other drugs, drowsiness can:

options.text: Help you be a better driver.

questions.explanation: Not sleeping enough causes poor driving. Like drugs and alcohol, being tired slows your reaction time, reduces awareness, and hurts your judgment.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should:

options.text: Turn on your high beam headlights.
Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
Speed up to avoid an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In fog, slow down and use your low beam lights. If the fog is very thick and you cannot see, pull off the road and wait for it to clear.

questions.question: If a tire suddenly goes flat while you are driving, you should:

options.text: Pump the brake pedal several times.
Slow down gradually without braking hard.
Press the brake pedal down as hard as you can.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually without braking hard.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly and keep the vehicle straight. Take your foot off the accelerator and do not brake hard. Let the vehicle slow down on its own. Use the brakes gently only if needed. Pull off the road when it is safe.

questions.question: Why should drivers give extra space to children on bicycles?

options.text: Children do not have the same quick reflexes as adults.
Children are smaller and harder to see than adults.

questions.explanation: Children are unpredictable and hard to see. Watch carefully for children near schools, bus stops, playgrounds, parks, and ice cream trucks. Be aware that children on bikes may come onto the road without warning.

questions.question: To drive again after losing your license for not paying crash damages, you must file proof of money with the Secretary of State's office.
questions.explanation: Drivers without insurance who cause an accident with injury, death, or damage must give proof of payment to the Secretary of State's office. Not doing this may result in a suspended license.

questions.question: You see a green light, but traffic is blocking the intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Partially enter to claim your right-of-way.
Wait until you can cross the entire intersection safely.
Enter and wait for traffic to clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can cross the entire intersection safely.
questions.explanation: Even with a green light, do not enter the intersection unless you can get all the way across before the light turns red. Blocking the intersection can result in a ticket.

questions.question: This round sign warns you that you are approaching:
questions.explanation: A round sign means a railroad crossing is ahead. It is posted a few hundred feet before the tracks. Slow down, look, listen, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: This white sign means you cannot pass other vehicles:

options.text: Until after you pass the sign.

questions.explanation: A white rectangular sign shows you must follow the rule. This sign means you cannot pass any vehicles for any reason.

questions.question: Your reaction time slows down after:
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reactions, worsens your vision, and reduces alertness. As you drink more, your judgment gets worse and your driving skills decrease. You will have trouble judging distances, speeds, and how other vehicles are moving.

questions.question: What should you do if a child is riding a bicycle near your vehicle?

options.text: Expect the child to have full control of the bicycle.

questions.explanation: Children on bicycles can be unpredictable. They often make sudden direction changes without warning. Children and bicycles are small and hard to see.

questions.question: What should a driver do when pedestrians are in a crosswalk ahead?

options.text: Continue ahead. You have the right-of-way.
Wait for the pedestrians to cross.
Go around the pedestrians on the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the pedestrians to cross.
questions.explanation: Drivers must give the right-of-way to pedestrians in a crosswalk. Wait until the crosswalk is clear before moving forward.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn. You cannot turn your vehicle around to go the opposite direction at this location.

questions.question: When you see a stop sign, what should you do?

options.text: Check for vehicles in your direction only, then proceed.
Let all vehicles that arrive before or after you go first.
Stop completely and check all directions before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and check all directions before proceeding.
questions.explanation: At a stop sign, come to a full stop and look in all directions for traffic before moving forward.

questions.question: What should you do when driving through a construction zone?

options.text: Drive closer to the car in front of you.
Drive carefully and do not slow down to look at the work.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive carefully and do not slow down to look at the work.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down to look at construction work, as this causes traffic congestion. Drive carefully through the zone without stopping to watch.

questions.question: If you cannot merge safely, a yield sign means you must stop.
questions.explanation: When you must yield the right-of-way, you must also stop if you cannot safely merge into traffic.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you a steep hill is coming. Slow down and shift to a lower gear to control your speed and protect your brakes.

questions.question: What should drivers do when approaching a construction area?

options.text: Speed up to get through quickly.
Slow down, do not use your cell phone, and give workers the right-of-way.
Honk your horn several times to alert workers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, do not use your cell phone, and give workers the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: When approaching construction areas, slow down and do not use your phone (unless using hands-free). Give the right-of-way to workers and authorized vehicles. Move away from workers when possible and drive carefully.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road is slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign alerts you to conditions ahead. It warns that the road becomes slippery when it rains or is wet.

questions.question: What does this sign warn drivers about?

options.text: The right lane is ending and traffic must merge left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane is ending and traffic must merge left.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign alerts you that the number of lanes is decreasing ahead. Drivers must move left to merge with other traffic.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: One lane is ending. Move to the left.
A highway entrance ramp is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: One lane is ending. Move to the left.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign alerts drivers that a lane is ending ahead. Traffic must merge to the left.

questions.question: What does this yellow warning sign mean?

options.text: A school or school crossing is near.
Slow down and watch for children.

questions.explanation: This sign warns drivers to slow down and watch for children near schools.

questions.question: What should you do if you must make an emergency stop on an interstate?

options.text: Honk your horn to get other drivers' attention.
Get out and flag down the next car.
Pull to the shoulder, turn on emergency flashers, and stay in your car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the shoulder, turn on emergency flashers, and stay in your car.
questions.explanation: If you must stop on the shoulder, turn on your emergency flashers and stay in your vehicle. Standing or walking on an interstate is dangerous because of high-speed traffic.

questions.question: What sign has this shape and color?
questions.explanation: Triangle signs pointing downward mean yield. Slow down and stop if necessary. Stop at a marked stop line if one exists.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road will be slippery ahead.

questions.explanation: This sign shows a divided highway is beginning. Stay to the right of the median divider.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road may be slippery when wet. Drive carefully.

questions.question: What is the penalty for passing a stopped school bus?

options.text: License or vehicle registration suspension and a $300 fine.
$30 fine and 14-day suspension of driving privileges.

questions.correctAnswerText: License or vehicle registration suspension and a $300 fine.
questions.explanation: Passing a stopped school bus with flashing lights results in license suspension, a $300 fine, and community service. If someone else was driving, provide their name or your vehicle registration will be suspended for three months.

questions.question: Slowing down to look at accidents or unusual events:

options.text: Helps traffic flow by preventing crashes.

questions.explanation: Do not slow down to look at accidents. This "rubbernecking" causes traffic congestion.

questions.question: If your front right wheel leaves the road, you should ease off the accelerator, let the car slow down, and gently steer back onto the pavement.
questions.explanation: If your wheels drift off the road, grip the wheel firmly, ease off the gas, and brake gently. Check your mirrors and slowly steer back onto the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Reserved parking for people with disabilities.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reserved parking for people with disabilities.
questions.explanation: This sign marks parking spaces for vehicles with disability plates or placards.

questions.question: Which action is unlawful?

options.text: Pass another vehicle in a marked no passing zone.
Pass another vehicle over a railroad crossing.

questions.explanation: Do not pass when you cannot see far enough ahead to pass safely. Do not pass at street crossings, railroad crossings, in no passing zones, or when a solid yellow line is next to your lane. Do not pass if the car ahead stopped for a pedestrian or in work zones where passing is dangerous.

questions.question: A five-sided sign means:
questions.explanation: A five-sided sign warns drivers about a school zone. It may mark crosswalks in school areas where children or pedestrians may be present.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign shows that a pedestrian crosswalk is ahead.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when tires slide on water instead of gripping the road. What should you do in wet weather to prevent it?

options.text: Use cruise control to keep a steady speed.
Move to the shoulder as soon as it rains.

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on wet roads. Reduce your speed on wet pavement to prevent hydroplaning.

questions.question: A parent or legal guardian can cancel a minor's driver license anytime before age 18.
questions.explanation: A 16- or 17-year-old needs written permission from a parent or legal guardian to get a driver license. That parent or guardian can cancel the license anytime before the driver turns 18, for any reason.
